SMTO-TSK-0049 — This saved workflow is in an old format SMTO can't run

GUID: e098c582-5c6c-4f32-8dae-599f23da1bc1
Slug: recipe-legacy-intent-required
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • This workflow was saved in an older format that SMTO keeps for reference only. SMTO didn't start it, so nothing ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Workflows, select New workflow, and enter the request you want to repeat in Prompt. Or choose Save to workflow beside a chat prompt that did the job. A newly saved workflow uses the current format, which SMTO can run.
  2. On the new workflow's card, select Run now. This runs the up-to-date copy instead of the old one that SMTO only keeps for reference.
  3. If a schedule used the old workflow, open the new workflow's card and select Schedule to set the same timing. The old schedule still points at the old workflow and will keep failing.

What success looks like

  • The new workflow starts and opens a conversation showing its progress.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. You can keep the old workflow for reference; don't edit it to try to make it run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The native-intent recipe executor received a recipe whose artifact_kind is not native_intent and refused it ("Historical recipe preserved for reference").

What this means

  • The native-intent executor receives an artifact_kind other than native_intent and refuses historical formats through that entry point. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The native-intent executor receives an artifact_kind other than native_intent and refuses historical formats through that entry point.

How to diagnose it

  • Check artifact_kind and the supported executor; recorded workflows have their own path and should not be treated as obsolete solely by this guard.

How to fix it

  • Run saved_request_v1 and recorded_workflow_v1 recipes through their own invocation paths, not recipes.native.invocation/execute_recipe. For a genuinely historical recipe, recreate it: run the work once, then capture a new workflow (Save to workflow, or Teach workflow from this run for a learned workflow) and run that new revision.
  • Use the supported interface for this artifact kind, or capture a reviewed new intent from genuinely historical formats.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The item uses its matching supported interface, or a reviewed new intent is captured where necessary.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
